title: AIR AI Governance Agentic Overlay
description: Conditional referential overlay for AI-enabled systems that select tools, execute multi-step actions, change external state, or receive delegated authority. It adds action-boundary, checkpoint, containment, rollback, and accountability requirements without treating the overlay or system as an autonomous AIR agent.

activation_triggers: The AI selects or calls tools.
The AI executes multi-step actions rather than only recommending.
The AI can create, modify, send, delete, purchase, publish, deploy, or otherwise affect external state.
Human review occurs after action or only by exception.
The system delegates tasks to other models, services, or automated components.
non_triggers: Single-turn drafting with no tool or external effect.
Read-only analysis with no delegated action.
Human-controlled execution where every effect is separately reviewed before action.

terminology.delegated_authority: Permission for an AI-enabled system to select or execute actions within a defined scope.
terminology.action_boundary: Explicit allowed, conditionally allowed, and prohibited effects.
terminology.pre_effect_checkpoint: Human or policy review before an external effect occurs.
terminology.post_effect_review: Review after action; not equivalent to pre-authorization.
terminology.containment: Controls that limit scope, duration, permissions, resources, and blast radius.
terminology.rollback: A tested means to reverse or compensate for an effect where possible.
terminology.kill_switch: A mechanism to stop further action; its existence does not prove effectiveness.

domain_constraints: Define the exact tools, permissions, resources, data, environments, and external effects.
Use least privilege and time-bounded authority.
Separate recommendation, preparation, approval, and execution authority.

Require pre-effect human approval for high-impact, irreversible, financial, legal, security, privacy, public, or safety-relevant effects unless a separately approved policy permits bounded automation.
Log action requests, policy decisions, approvals, tool calls, outcomes, failures, and rollback attempts.
Test containment, termination, and rollback rather than documenting them only.
Do not allow acknowledgement to waive legal accountability or prohibited action boundaries.
common_failure_modes: Agent label used to hide unclear authority.
Human review only after irreversible effect.
No distinction between drafting and executing.
Action logs omit denied, partial, or failed actions.
unsafe_assumptions: A sandbox prevents all external harm.
A human in the loop reviewed the actual effect.
A model refusal policy is an execution control.
Read access cannot create sensitive downstream effects.
Delegation transfers accountability to the system.

classes: current platform permission and tool documentation
security threat models and test evidence
current official AI governance and cybersecurity guidance

claim_boundaries: An action-control design does not prove safe autonomous operation.
Logging does not prove prevention, correctness, or accountability sufficiency.
A tested narrow action does not validate untested tools, permissions, environments, or use cases.
Final deployment and residual-risk acceptance remain human-owned.
non_goals: Prove tool safety, containment, or rollback effectiveness without tests.
Replace security, legal, safety, privacy, or operational approval.
